stem: The elements in Group 2 and their compounds show various trends in their physical and chemical properties.

parts.label: (a)(i)
parts.stem:
The graph below shows the radius values of the atoms and $2+$ ions of the elements in Group 2.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}
parts.text: Explain why both lines show a steady increase in the values of the radii down the group.

parts.label: (a)(ii)
parts.text: State and explain which line represents the atomic radii and which represents the ionic radii.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem:
$\mathbf{L}$ is a salt of a Group 2 element $\mathbf{M}$. When $\mathbf{L}$ is heated strongly a brown gas is observed and a white solid remains.

The white solid dissolves in water to form a colourless solution of the metal hydroxide $\mathbf{M}\text{(OH)}_2$.

Addition of dilute sulfuric acid to this colourless solution produces a dense white precipitate.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Identify the element $\mathbf{M}$ and write an ionic equation for the formation of the white precipitate with sulfuric acid.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: Give the formula of salt $\mathbf{L}$ and use it to write an equation for the thermal decomposition of salt $\mathbf{L}$.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.stem: Calcium carbonate and calcium hydroxide can both be used in agriculture to neutralise acidic soils.
parts.text: Write ionic equations for the neutralisation of acid by each of calcium hydroxide and calcium carbonate.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: Suggest and explain why calcium carbonate is a better choice than calcium hydroxide for this purpose in areas of high rainfall.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: Magnesium reacts with both cold water and steam.
parts.text: Give the formula of the magnesium-containing product of each of these reactions.
